subject: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks (next tests)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-06T15:23:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed next benchmark tests

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

Key takeaways from the discovery call:
- Globex is focused on matching the hyperscaler endpoint for latency while reducing per-token cost.
- Primary workloads: chat-like single-turn requests (avg 60 tokens) and batch embedding/summary jobs (longer sequences up to 2k tokens).
- SLOs: p95 < 250ms for interactive flows; throughput targets for batch jobs ~20k tokens/sec at peak.

Initial competitive observations (from the small dataset you shared):
- Hyperscaler baseline (their managed endpoint): p95 ~380ms, p99 ~1.2s on 1K token runs; tokens/sec during throughput test ~18k.
- Redwood hosted baseline (our quick runs): p95 ~210ms, p99 ~540ms; tokens/sec ~22k. These are preliminary — need matched configs.

Proposed next tests (A/B, identical model + prompt set):
1) Low-latency single-stream (no batching): measure p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm cache.
2) Throughput sweep: batch sizes {1,4,8,16,32}, measure tokens/sec and per-token cost.
3) Long-context stress: 1k/2k/4k tokens, p95/p99.
4) Quantization/variant test: float16 vs 4-bit (if you can run quantized variants).
5) Canary in your environment: run a short smoke test behind Globex's network to validate network/egress differences.

What we need from Globex to proceed:
- Baseline test credentials or a short-lived API key if you'd like us to run tests from your account (or we can provide scripts for your infra to run).
- Confirmation of the exact model variant to match (model name & tokenizer settings).
- Permission to share aggregated benchmark results with your infra team and leadership.

I attached a short runbook and the script we typically use for A/B tests. If you prefer, Vivek (cc'd) can lead the technical setup.

Next step: propose a 60-min technical runbook review + schedule the A/B runs next week (Tue or Wed). What works best for you?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-bench-runbook.pdf (runbook), grpc-benchmark-script.sh (script)

2) Were your Redwood runs using KV cache warm (i.e., repeated prompts leading to warm KVs) or strictly cold start?
3) For quantized runs, does Redwood support 4-bit quant on your hosted API, or would that require a Dedicated/private deployment?

We're happy to schedule the runbook review. Tue (2026-10-13) morning PT works for Samira and me.

Attaching the CSV with our measurement points.
—Alex

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next benchmark tests — technical notes

Looping in a few technical notes and a suggested test matrix. Happy to run these or walk your infra team through them.

Observed sources of variance between Redwood and hyperscaler endpoints:
- KV cache and warm token reuse: our continuous batching + KV cache often yields large wins for repeated conversational contexts (p95 improvement). Cold-start single-shot requests are closer to hyperscaler numbers.
- Kernel selection and sequence-length-specific optimizations: we pick kernels by sequence distribution which improves throughput at common lengths (<=512 tokens).
- Networking and TLS overhead: if tests run outside your VPC region, p99 can spike due to egress latency.

Proposed detailed test matrix (we recommend automating via the attached script):
A) Single-stream latency: batch=1, concurrency=1, sequences 32/64/128 tokens, cold vs warm (10 warm iterations). Measure p50/p95/p99, median tokens/sec for 60s.
B) Throughput sweep: concurrency sweep {1,2,4,8,16}, batch sizes {1,4,8,16,32}, sequences 60 tokens, measure sustained tokens/sec and 95th latency.
C) Long-context: sequences 1k/2k/4k, batch=1 and batch=4, measure memory utilization + throughput.
D) Quantization variants: float16 baseline, 4-bit quant (if you run quant locally or via Dedicated).

Preliminary numbers (matching the CSV Alex attached):
- Redwood (float16, warm cache, batch=4, seq=60): p50 36ms, p95 210–230ms, p99 540ms, tokens/sec ~22k.
- Hyperscaler (float16, warm cache, batch=4, seq=60): p50 58ms, p95 370–400ms, p99 1.1–1.3s, tokens/sec ~18k.

Action items for the run:
- We'll standardize tokenization and prompt templates to make results apples-to-apples.
- We'll run both endpoints from the same client location (your infra) to eliminate network egress variance — preference: run in Globex VPC or provide a short-lived key for us to run from a nearby region.
- We'll produce an A/B report with plots (latency CDFs, tokens/sec vs batch, cost per 1M tokens).

Links: runbook + Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-globex-runbook
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-4782

Let me know if you'd like us to include Dedicated-reserved runs (we can provision a small Dedicated pool for a short trial if you want to test quantized variants and more predictable throughput).

—Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
